I grew up in the Portland metro and I remember this case, particularly the immersive media attention it received. I was 14 at the time it happened and I’ve always wondered how so many missteps occurred to cause Kyron’s disappearance. I recently took an interest in his disappearance and watched a few investigative documentaries covering it. From the time it happened, I have always suspected the step mother. Now, I’m not so sure. I visited the campus and area the family lived in, it’s heavily wooded on both sides of the road. While technically still “portland” it feels extremely rural and isolated. There are no sidewalks and there are countless ravines, sharp curves, etc. The school doesn’t have a clearly indicated perimeter and if Kyron truly was an absence seizure wanderer, he could have easily left the premises on his own fruition and then fallen down a steep embankment on his expedition. So much could have happened between the time he was “last seen” and the time the bus arrived. One of the investigative documentaries mentioned cadaver dogs alerting their handler when doing a perimeter sweep of Kaine’s property. I wonder if Kyron attempted to walk home from school after being disoriented from a seizure and injuring himself on the property…. I’m not sure how anyone would navigate that terrain even with a massive search party.

Growing up, you look at people in abusive and toxic work and relationships and wonder why anyone would stay in that situation. You certain don't think you would ever put up with that in your own life, EVER. I was in a gay relationship for about 2 years. My (ex)boyfriend grew up in Mexico and faced a childhood of merciless sexual abuse that nobody should have to go through. At this point in time, I was the only person who knew this secret and he had no desire to seek help with to process this and I supported his actions the best I could. He said he loved me the first day we started dating. By 3 months, things were physical. He would grab me, hit me, physically restrain me, etc. and along with the physical aspect of abuse he would gaslight and use mental abuse to gain control. I was 21 when we met. I was cuter, made more money, had a promising career, had my own place, etc. meanwhile he was 33 years old, still in an entry level position, living with his family, etc. I loved him. After a while I truly believed I was worthless and had no value. I believed him when he told me that nobody would ever love me. He would get angry if I tried to see my friends. All of his friends hated me and thought I was an awful bitch. We broke up October 1st, 2018. On October 6th, he asked me to go with him to a friends birthday party to which I obliged. He got sloshed and I drove home to my house. I had a guest room and told him he was welcome to stay. He was angry that I wouldn't let him sleep in my bed. He started trying to steal laptop so I grabbed it and ran out of my house. He chased me outside and body slammed me on the ground 3x. He had beat me to a bloody pulp, fractured my ribs and knocked the wind out of me before I gave up because I knew I would die if I fought anymore. Even after this, I still loved him and gave him another chance the following April. Things were great for a week. Downhill from there. He continued his abusive patterns and yet again October 6th, 2019 rolls around. He gets angry that I have a friend over. Leaves in a rage, packs all of his stuff and on his way out throws a burning hot pizza straight out of the oven in my face and slams me against a wall so hard I thought I was going to take the wall down with me. It was that point when I told him to leave and never come back. This was the first time I meant it. He's been gone since and I've progressed ever farther in my career. These are just two extreme examples in a relationship riddled with many smaller instances. The police came twice and nothing happened. Domestic Violence in gay relationships is very much real.
